meta.description: Analyzes CRISPR drug-modifier (chemogenomic) screens with drugZ (Colic et al. 2019 Genome Med), a bidirectional Z-score method identifying synthetic-lethal sensitizing genes and resistance-conferring suppressor genes from vehicle vs drug comparisons.

scientific_integrity.detail: Citations (Colic 2019 Genome Med, Olivieri 2020 Cell, Behan 2019 Nature) are real and match drugZ's actual provenance; no fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics across any of the 7 outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely a screen-analysis research tool; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or individual-patient claims anywhere, including the new synergy-screen input (Input 7).

methodological_ground.detail: Core method (bidirectional Z, vehicle-anchored not Day-0) re-verified correct; the previously-broken essentials-exclusion example and previously-pseudocode dose-consistency logic are now both real, correct, runnable code, verified against planted ground truth.

code_usability.detail: All 7 CLI/code paths documented in SKILL.md/usage-guide/examples ran without syntax errors or missing dependencies. The Input-2 P0 from the pre-fix audit (essentials-exclusion silently excluding 0 genes) is fixed and now self-verifying via an assert in examples/run_drugz.py.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness/appropriateness strong and unchanged. Correctness no longer docked: examples/run_drugz.py Step 2 now parses CEGv2.txt correctly (verified: excludes 646/684 genes) and asserts non-zero exclusion. Half-point-equivalent still missing: no worked example demonstrates the new half_window_size guidance end-to-end on a small table.

reliability.note: Both pre-fix P0/P1 reliability gaps are substantively fixed: the essentials-exclusion no-op now fails loudly (assert) instead of exiting 0 silently, and the half_window_size/library-size crash is now documented with the exact error text and a concrete fix (verified: IndexError at default on 200 guides, clean run at --half_window_size 50). Docked because that guidance lives only in the Algorithm-section prose, not in the Common Errors quick-reference table -- see recommendations.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew modestly (~254 to ~299 lines) to add the half_window_size paragraph and the rewritten -r section; still linear, no redundant steps, reasonable progressive disclosure.

agent_usability.note: Terminology/output-column documentation remains an exact match to real drugZ output. Error Prevention improved: Failure Modes table's 'Unstable hits' entry was correctly corrected to state a rerun on identical input cannot demonstrate instability (verified: two reruns are byte-identical). Still docked one point for the Common Errors table gap noted under Reliability.

human_usability.note: Quick Start / Example Prompts unchanged and strong. Forgiveness improved: the -r footgun that previously failed silently now fails loudly via an assert in the shipped example, which is a real usability improvement, not just a correctness fix.

security.note: No credentials or PHI involved. Input Validation improved: examples/run_drugz.py now validates that -r's gene list actually removed genes (assert removed) instead of trusting an unvalidated join, closing the exact hole that produced the pre-fix P0.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide/examples split, unchanged. Testability improved: the essentials-exclusion example now has a self-check (gene-count diff) that would have caught its own pre-fix bug; the dose-consistency function is now real code that can be unit-tested.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description, explicit Related Skills cross-references, and CLI determinism now independently reconfirmed (byte-identical reruns). Escape Hatches still thin: no guidance on what to do when a run crashes or replicate Pearson falls below 0.85 beyond listing it as a checklist item -- unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

Built a low/mid/high 3-dose count table (low = geometric mean of vehicle and the mid-dose arm, matching the fix log's own method) and ran drugZ once per dose vs the same vehicle. Copied SKILL.md's dose_consistent_hits() function character-for-character and called it on the three output files.

assertions.text: SKILL.md's dose-consistency code is real, runnable Python, not a commented-out sketch
assertions.note: dose_consistent_hits() ran unmodified, no syntax edits needed.

assertions.text: It recovers the planted sensitizers as dose-consistent hits
assertions.note: 6/6 planted sensitizers returned (OSTM1, CER1, IL18R1, CCDC89, GALNT11, CFL2), all with normZ growing in magnitude low->mid->high (monotonic=True).

assertions.text: It does not report false positives among non-planted genes
assertions.note: hits set == planted set exactly; 0 extra genes.

assertions.text: A concrete numeric consistency rule is stated, not just 'consistent direction'
assertions.note: SKILL.md states: same normZ sign at every dose AND fdr<0.05 at the top dose; |normZ| growth is supporting evidence only, matching what the function implements.

inputs.label: NEW: T3 determinism check -- rerun drugZ twice on identical input
inputs.note: executed: true. Not in the pre-fix audit. Directly tests the fix log's claim that drugZ has no sampling step or seed and the Skill's rewritten 'Unstable hits' failure mode, which now states a same-input rerun cannot demonstrate instability.

assertions.text: Two identical drugZ invocations on the same input produce byte-identical output files
assertions.note: filecmp.cmp(shallow=False) True; max |normZ| diff between reruns = 0.0.

assertions.text: SKILL.md's failure-mode text matches this empirical behavior (no overclaimed non-determinism)
assertions.note: 'drugZ has no sampling step and no seed: identical input gives a byte-identical output file, so a rerun is not a stability check.' -- verified true.

assertions.text: The Skill points to a real stability check instead (replicate hold-out / guide bootstrapping)
assertions.note: Fix text: 'check stability by holding out a replicate or bootstrapping the guides yourself; or use MAGeCK MLE.'

assertions.text: T3 Result Determinism veto criterion is satisfied
assertions.note: No output variance on identical input at any temperature-equivalent setting; CLI tool, not an LLM sampling step.

inputs.note: executed: false (Mode A reasoning task, not code). Prompt: 'I have a Drug A + Drug B combination screen (single arm each drug, plus the combo, vs vehicle) and want to find genes whose loss is synergistically lethal with the combination. Can I just run drugZ on combo-vs-vehicle?' Checked the Skill's own guidance for whether it correctly scopes drugZ's applicability here rather than presenting a per-drug drugZ run as sufficient for synergy detection.

assertions.text: The Skill does not claim drugZ can detect synergy/interaction effects on its own
assertions.note: SKILL.md's comparison table: 'Synergy / antagonism detection: Limited (per-drug calling only)' vs 'MAGeCK MLE: YES (interaction term in MLE)'; no synergy-score column exists in drugZ's documented output.

assertions.text: The Skill redirects a synergy-detection question to MAGeCK MLE with an interaction term
assertions.note: usage-guide's Decision Cheat Sheet: 'Synergy / antagonism | MAGeCK MLE with interaction term', matched verbatim in SKILL.md's comparison table.

assertions.text: The Skill still offers a constructive drugZ-based first pass rather than a bare refusal
assertions.note: 'Reconciliation' section: run both methods; drugZ-only hits at low LFC flagged as needing orthogonal validation -- a per-drug drugZ run remains useful as one input, just not sufficient alone for synergy.

assertions.text: No fabricated statistical claim is introduced to answer the out-of-scope part of the question
assertions.note: No invented synergy metric or p-value; the answer stays within what drugZ's real output columns support.

key_strengths: The pre-fix P0 is genuinely fixed and self-verifying, not papered over: run side by side, the corrected -r parsing excludes 646/684 CEGv2 genes (18,054 -> 17,408 output rows) while the old broken join, on identical input, still excludes 0/684 and is byte-identical to the unfiltered run -- confirming the original defect was real and the fix targets it directly.

The dose-response section's code is now genuinely runnable: SKILL.md's dose_consistent_hits(), copied character-for-character with no edits, recovered 6/6 planted sensitizers across a 3-dose synthetic screen with zero false positives.

drugZ's determinism claim is independently verified, not just asserted: two full reruns of the same 71,090-guide input produced byte-identical output files (max |normZ| diff = 0.0), matching the Skill's corrected 'Unstable hits' failure-mode text.

The Skill correctly scopes its own limits rather than overclaiming: presented with a combinatorial drug-synergy question outside drugZ's documented strengths, its own comparison table and decision cheat sheet redirect to MAGeCK MLE with an interaction term instead of forcing an inappropriate per-drug drugZ analysis.

Unchanged, already-strong behavior held up under re-test: the canonical run and the Day-0-vs-vehicle failure-mode diagnosis reproduced the pre-fix audit's exact numbers (12/12 planted hits; 509 vs 6 spurious genes under Day-0).

recommendations.title: Common Errors table still lacks a half_window_size/IndexError row
recommendations.problem: The pre-fix audit's own P1 recommendation proposed adding a Common Errors row for 'IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds'. The fixer instead documented the fix as prose (per the fix log: 'New paragraph after the algorithm'), and that prose is accurate and complete. But the shipped SKILL.md's Common Errors table (6 rows: No hits / Hits dominated by essentials / Unstable hits / Drug-target as suppressor / MAGeCK-drugZ disagreement / Inconsistent between doses) still has no row for this crash, so an agent that jumps straight to that quick-reference table after hitting the error will not find the fix there.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix addressed the substance (documenting the guide-count / half_window_size relationship) via Algorithm-section prose rather than the Common Errors table the original recommendation suggested; both are legitimate documentation choices, but only the table is a quick-lookup surface for this specific crash message.
recommendations.fix: Add a row to the Common Errors table: 'IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds | half_window_size too large for total guide count | set --half_window_size to ~1/4 of total guides; see Algorithm section'.

recommendations.title: Escape Hatches for a crashed run or low replicate concordance remain thin
recommendations.problem: Beyond the checklist item 'Replicate Pearson >0.85', there is still no guidance on what to do when a run crashes generally or when replicate concordance falls below that threshold -- unchanged from the pre-fix audit.
recommendations.root_cause: The fix round targeted the three findings explicitly reported (essentials exclusion, half_window_size, dose pseudocode) and did not extend to this pre-existing, lower-priority gap.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'If replicate Pearson <0.85' subsection: hold out the worst replicate and re-run, or flag the screen as QC-failed before trusting drugZ's small-effect sensitivity, which amplifies noise on poor-concordance data.
